theorem.statement:
Let \(\overline c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\) be the certified outward critical value constructed by the attainable Gaussian-tube calibration handle, and define
\[
 \widetilde C_N=\{b\in\mathcal B:T_N(b)\le
 \overline c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\inf_{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M}
 P_N\{\beta\in\widetilde C_N\}=1-\alpha,                                   \tag{23}
\]
simultaneously at zero amplitude, bounded local amplitudes, diverging physically attainable amplitudes, exponent endpoints, \(|\lambda_N|^{-1}\)-local endpoint approaches, the \(d=1\) elbow window, and nonconvergent allowed design sequences.  The Gaussian reference quantile extends uniformly continuously across the bounded, tangent-plane, and endpoint-half-plane compactification.  Given convergent outward rational interval enclosures of the fixed declared nuisance compactum and observed coordinates, the finite subdivision and Gaussian cubature algorithm returns
\[
 c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}le
 \overline c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}le
 c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}+N^{-1},                                        \tag{24}
\]
so its approximation is certified from above.  Finally, for a constant independent of the law and design,
\[
 \operatorname{diam}(\widetilde C_N)\le C_\alpha N^{-1/2}                   \tag{25}
\]
pathwise for all sufficiently large \(N\).
theorem.proof_tex:
Define the centered standardized experiment variable
\[
 Z_N=\sqrt{\frac N\gamma}
 \{m_N-\beta\mathbf1-B_Nq_N(p)\}.
\]
Because \(\mathcal C_N\) is a cone, multiplication of every line loading by the positive number \(\sqrt{N/\gamma}\) leaves it unchanged.  Consequently the statistic at the true slope has the exact representation
\[
 T_N(\beta)
 =\frac{\gamma}{\widehat\gamma_N}
 d_{H_N}(Z_N+\lambda_Nq_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2.                                \tag{26}
\]
The uniform-experiment theorem gives
\[
 \sup_{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M}
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\{\mathcal L(Z_N),N_3(0,H_N)\}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \frac{\widehat\gamma_N}{\gamma}\longrightarrow1                         \tag{27}
\]
uniformly in probability.  Positivity and compactness of the nuisance scales bound \(\gamma\) above and away from zero.

We first upgrade (27) at the changing profile boundaries.  The map
\[
 z\longmapsto d_{H_N}(z+\lambda q_N(p),\mathcal C_N)                         \tag{28}
\]
is Lipschitz, with a constant bounded uniformly by the eigenvalue bounds on \(H_N\), regardless of \(\lambda\).  Approximate the indicator of \(( -\infty,r]\) by upper and lower piecewise-linear functions with transition width \(\delta\), and compose them with (28).  The bounded-Lipschitz error in (27), multiplied by at most \(C/\delta\), tends to zero for each fixed \(\delta\).  The difference between the two approximations is bounded by a Gaussian probability in a \(C\delta\)-neighborhood of a squared-distance level.  The anti-concentration relation (9), followed by \(\delta\downarrow0\), therefore proves
\[
 \sup_{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M}\sup_{0\le x\le M}
 \left|
 P_N\{d_{H_N}(Z_N+\lambda_Nq_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2\le x\}
 -\Pr\{d_{H_N}(G_N+\lambda_Nq_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2\le x\}
 \right|\longrightarrow0                                                    \tag{29}
\]
for every fixed \(M\).  The reference distance is bounded above by the distance to the true nuisance line, as in (22), so it is uniformly tight.  The same is true for the first probability by (27).  Combining this tightness, (9), and the second relation in (27) shows that multiplication by \(\gamma/\widehat\gamma_N\) in (26) does not change (29).

By the finite-design lemma, every physical reference law has rejection probability at most \(\alpha\) at \(c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\), and some legal parameter tuple attains equality.  The outward error in (24) and uniform anti-concentration imply
\[
 \inf_{(\lambda,p)\in\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}}
 \Pr\{d_{H_N}(G_N+\lambda q_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2
 \le\overline c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\}
 =1-\alpha+o(1).                                                             \tag{30}
\]
The lower bound in (30) follows from outward calibration.  For the reverse bound choose a maximizing legal tuple; at the exact critical value its probability is \(1-\alpha\), and (9) makes the probability added by the interval of width \(N^{-1}\) vanish uniformly.  Such maximizing tuples may vary with \(N\), which is permitted by the triangular-array model and is essential at zero amplitude and the elbow.  Applying (29) to (26) and (30) proves (23).  The regime lemma verifies that the physical sets used here include exactly the stated dimension-dependent local, divergent, and transition sequences; the compactification lemma covers their tangent and endpoint limits.

We now give the certification argument.  It is deterministic conditional on the observed design.  The exact functions \(q_N(r)\) are finite sums of \(s^{2r}=\exp(2r\log s)\), and \(H_N\) is a finite matrix of observed distances and weights.  Outward rational intervals for the coordinates therefore produce convergent outward intervals for \(q_N,q_N',q_N''\), \(H_N^{-1}\), and all quadratic objectives.  The determinant constraint reduces, by (3), to minimizing the explicit positive radial function
\[
 c_Xc_W\frac{(\alpha_C^2+r^2)^{2p+d}}
 {(\alpha_X^2+r^2)^{(d+1)/2}(\alpha_W^2+r^2)^{(d+1)/2}},qquad r\ge0.         \tag{31}
\]
Its uniform asymptotic order \(r^{4p-2}\), with \(4p_{\min}-2>0\), supplies a certified finite tail cutoff; interval subdivision on the remaining compact radial interval and on the supplied nested covers of \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm{nuis}}\) gives nested outward covers of \(\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}\).  Boundary boxes are retained, so every reported upper bound remains valid even when legality is not decided at a subdivision boundary.

Write \(G_N=H_N^{1/2}Z\), where \(Z\) has three independent standard normal coordinates.  The elementary integration-by-parts bound
\[
 \Pr(|Z_k|>R)\le2e^{-R^2/2}
\]
and a union bound make the omitted probability outside \([-R,R]^3\) at most \(6e^{-R^2/2}\).  On this cube and the compact physical set, the nearest line loading may be restricted to a finite interval: comparison with loading zero and the lower bounds on \(\|q_N(r)\|\) and on the eigenvalues of \(H_N\) give \(|b|\le C_{N,R}\).  Subdivide the finite box in \((\lambda,p,r,b,Z)\).  For each \((\lambda,p,Z)\)-box, interval upper evaluations at candidate \((r,b)\)-boxes certify cells lying inside the distance event, while interval lower evaluations over all \((r,b)\)-boxes certify cells outside it.  Integrating the product normal density over classified \(Z\)-boxes, with outward one-dimensional normal-cdf intervals, gives lower and upper bounds for every reference distribution function, uniformly over each physical parameter box.

As the mesh tends to zero and \(R\to\infty\), the probability of unclassified boxes tends to zero uniformly.  Indeed, an unclassified limiting point lies on a distance level, and a contrary positive residual mass would violate (9).  The same subdivision over \((\lambda,p)\) therefore gives convergent lower and upper bounds on
\[
 \inf_{(\lambda,p)\in\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}}
 \Pr\{d_{H_N}(G_N+\lambda q_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2\le x\}.                    \tag{32}
\]
If \(x>c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\), compactness, strict increase, and continuity give that (32) is strictly larger than \(1-\alpha\); if \(x<c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\), a maximizing parameter has probability strictly smaller than \(1-\alpha\).  Certified bisection thus terminates with a bracket of any prescribed positive width, in particular \(N^{-1}\).  Taking its upper endpoint and using (21) for the cap proves (24).  Notice that refinement is simultaneous in \(p\) and \(\lambda\); no coarse exponent grid or simulation error is hidden in the certificate.

Finally, take \(b_1,b_2\in\widetilde C_N\).  Choose corresponding cone points \(z_1,z_2\) within an arbitrarily small error of their profile minima.  The triangle inequality gives
\[
 \|(b_1-b_2)\mathbf1+z_1-z_2\|
 \le2\sqrt{\lambda_{\max}(H_N)
             \widehat\gamma_N\overline c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}/N}
 +o(1).
\]
Moment separation bounds the left side below by \(c_\star|b_1-b_2|\).  The deterministic clipping bounds \(\widehat\gamma_N\), while (21) and (24) bound the critical value.  Letting the optimization error vanish proves (25), with the empty-set diameter defined as zero.  This completes the construction and the attainable calibration proof.
theorem.justification: The theorem replaces conservative calibration by an attainable, design-specific Gaussian critical value while preserving uniform exact lower-envelope coverage through the singular face \(A=0\).
theorem.gap: Generic weak-identification theory does not supply the compactification, uniform anti-concentration, physical-regime restriction, or certified continuum optimization for this changing spatial cone.
theorem.consumer: Conditional on the stated no-nugget Mat\'ern and deterministic quasi-uniform design diagnostics, the result supplies attainable homogeneous-slope confidence sets for the county-centroid setting of Burman, Ogburn and Datta.

added_lemmas.statement:
Assume that the model class is nonempty and put
\[
 R_N(p)=\sqrt N\,h_N^{2p-1}.
\]
Then \(0<\rho\le1\), and every \((\lambda,p)\in\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}\) satisfies
\[
 \lambda=\frac{\sqrt N B_N}{\sqrt\gamma}
 =\frac{A K_d(p)}{\sqrt{c_Xc_W}}R_N(p),
 \qquad |\lambda|\le C R_N(p).
\]
If \(0<\rho<1\), there is \(c>0\), independent of \(N\), the design, and \(p\), such that
\[
 [-cR_N(p),cR_N(p)]\times\{p\}
 \subseteq\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}
 \subseteq[-CR_N(p),CR_N(p)]\times\{p\}.
\]
If \(\rho=1\), instead \(\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}=\{0\}\times[p_{\min},p_{\max}]\).  Under strict slack \(0<\rho<1\), the following regimes result.  For \(d=1\), fixed \(p<3/4\) permits bounded local sequences and diverging sequences of either sign up to the physical order \(R_N(p)\), while every fixed sufficiently small nonzero \(A\) gives \(|\lambda|\to\infty\); at \(p=3/4\) all physical \(\lambda\)'s are bounded; and for fixed \(p>3/4\), \(\sup|\lambda|\to0\).  If
\[
 p_N=\frac34+\frac{z_N}{\log N},\qquad |z_N|\le C_z,
\]
then, with \(\kappa_N=Nh_N\),
\[
 R_N(p_N)=\kappa_N^{1/2+2z_N/\log N}e^{-2z_N},
\]
so the entire logarithmic transition window is bounded above and away from zero.  For \(d=2\), \(R_N(p)\to\infty\) uniformly over \(p\in[p_{\min},p_{\max}]\); hence every fixed exponent permits bounded local sequences and sub-capacity diverging sequences, including such sequences generated by \(A_N\to0\), and every fixed sufficiently small nonzero \(A\) produces divergence.

For the allowed exact affine-stencil designs, the family \(\{q_N\}\) is bounded in \(C^2([p_{\min},p_{\max}];\mathbb R^3)\), and the matrices \(H_N\) range over a compact subset of the positive-definite cone.  Every sequence of translated profile cones
\[
 \mathcal C_N-\lambda_Nq_N(p_N)
\]
has a subsequence converging locally in Hausdorff distance either to a translated limiting cone when \(\lambda_N\) is bounded, or, when \(|\lambda_N|\to\infty\), to a limiting tangent plane or an endpoint tangent half-plane of the form
\[
 \{a q(p_0)+tq'(p_0):a\in\mathbb R,\ t\in I\},
\]
where \(I=\mathbb R\) or \(I\) is a closed half-line; finite values of \(|\lambda_N|\operatorname{dist}(p_N,\{p_{\min},p_{\max}\})\) give the half-line offsets.  For every finite \(M\), these limits imply the uniform Gaussian anti-concentration relation
\[
 \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\ 
 \sup_{N,\mathcal S_N,\lambda,p}\ \sup_{0\le x\le M}
 \Pr\!\left(\left|d_{H_N}(G_N+\lambda q_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2-x\right|
 \le\varepsilon\right)=0.                                                    \tag{9}
\]
The corresponding quantile functions extend continuously, and hence uniformly continuously, to this bounded-amplitude/tangent/endpoint compactification, including nonconvergent allowed design sequences.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
All normalized within-stencil distances are bounded above by a fixed constant and, off the diagonal, bounded away from zero by the separation assumption.  The proof of the affine-stencil lemma gives uniformly bounded weights, fixed stencil cardinality, and denominators bounded away from zero.  Differentiating a nonzero term \(r^{2p}\) zero, one, or two times introduces only the bounded factors \(1\), \(2\log r\), and \(4(\log r)^2\); diagonal terms are identically zero.  The quotient rule and positivity of \(P_\star\) therefore give
\[
 \sup_N\sup_{p\in[p_{\min},p_{\max}]}
 \bigl(\|q_N(p)\|+\|q_N'(p)\|+\|q_N''(p)\|\bigr)<\infty.                 \tag{10}
\]
The eigenvalue bounds in the uniform-experiment theorem similarly place \(H_N\) in a compact subset of the positive-definite cone.

For completeness, (10) itself gives the needed sequential compactness without importing an empirical-process theorem.  On each finite rational grid, boundedness permits a convergent subsequence.  A diagonal choice over successively finer grids, together with
\[
 \|q_N'(u)-q_N'(v)\|\le C|u-v|,
 \qquad
 q_N(v)-q_N(u)=\int_u^v q_N'(r)\,dr,                                         \tag{11}
\]
extends the grid limits uniformly to a continuously differentiable curve \(q\), with \(q_N\to q\) in \(C^1\).  A further subsequence has \(H_N\to H\), where \(H\) remains positive definite.

The divided-difference argument in the moment-separation lemma also yields constants \(c,C>0\) such that
\[
 c\le \|q_N(p)\|\le C,
 \qquad
 \|q_N(p)\times d_N(p,u)\|\ge c,
 \quad
 d_N(p,u)=
 \begin{cases}
 \{q_N(u)-q_N(p)\}/(u-p),&u\ne p,\\
 q_N'(p),&u=p.
 \end{cases}                                                                 \tag{12}
\]
Indeed, the determinant of \([\mathbf1,q_N(p),d_N(p,u)]\) is uniformly separated from zero and all three columns are bounded.  In particular,
\[
 \|q_N(p)\times q_N(u)\|\ge c|p-u|.                                         \tag{13}
\]

Consider first a bounded sequence \(\lambda_N\).  After taking subsequences, \(\lambda_N\to\lambda\), \(p_N\to p_0\), and (11) holds.  Coercivity from the first bound in (12) shows that points of \(\mathcal C_N\) lying in a fixed ball have bounded line loading.  Uniform convergence of \(q_N\) then proves local Hausdorff convergence
\[
 \mathcal C_N-\lambda_Nq_N(p_N)
 \longrightarrow
 \{bq(r):b\in\mathbb R,\ r\in[p_{\min},p_{\max}]\}
 -\lambda q(p_0).                                                            \tag{14}
\]

Now suppose \(|\lambda_N|\to\infty\), and take a subsequence on which its sign is constant and \(p_N\to p_0\).  If
\[
 b_Nq_N(r_N)-\lambda_Nq_N(p_N)                                               \tag{15}
\]
stays bounded, (12)--(13) first imply \(|b_N|\asymp|\lambda_N|\) and \(|r_N-p_N|=O(|\lambda_N|^{-1})\).  Writing \(a_N=b_N-\lambda_N\) and \(t_N=b_N(r_N-p_N)\), and using the divided difference in (12), (15) becomes
\[
 a_Nq_N(p_N)+t_Nd_N(p_N,r_N).                                                \tag{16}
\]
The linear independence in (12) makes both \(a_N\) and \(t_N\) bounded whenever (16) is bounded.  Conversely, every convergent allowed pair \((a_N,t_N)\) in (16) is obtained by taking \(b_N=\lambda_N+a_N\) and \(r_N=p_N+t_N/b_N\).  Thus the local limit is
\[
 \{a q(p_0)+tq'(p_0):a\in\mathbb R,\ t\in I\}.                            \tag{17}
\]
If both scaled endpoint distances diverge, \(I=\mathbb R\).  If, for example, \(\lambda_N>0\), \(p_N\to p_{\min}\), and \(\lambda_N(p_N-p_{\min})\to\tau<\infty\), then the constraint \(r_N\ge p_{\min}\) becomes \(t\ge-\tau\).  The upper endpoint and negative-sign cases reverse the appropriate inequality.  These are exactly the asserted tangent half-planes.  Equations (14)--(17) prove compactification, including endpoint approaches of order \(|\lambda_N|^{-1}\).

We next verify atomlessness rather than assume it.  Every translated cone in (14) is the image of the two-dimensional parameterization \((b,r)\mapsto bq(r)-\lambda q(p_0)\); on bounded \(b\)-sets this map is Lipschitz.  Hence it has three-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero, as follows directly by covering its parameter rectangle by \(O(\delta^{-2})\) squares whose images lie in balls of radius \(C\delta\), of total volume \(O(\delta)\).  The planes and half-planes in (17) also have zero volume.

Fix any one of these closed sets \(K\) and a positive-definite metric \(H\).  For \(r>0\), a point at distance \(r\) from a regular point of the parameterized surface must lie on a metric-normal line, by differentiating the squared distance in its two parameter directions.  Such points are covered, on bounded pieces away from the cone vertex and parameter endpoints, by countably many two-dimensional Lipschitz offset charts.  Nearest points at the vertex are covered by a metric sphere, and nearest points at an endpoint edge are covered by two-dimensional normal half-sphere charts.  The same \(O(\delta)\) covering argument gives
\[
 \operatorname{Leb}_3\{x:d_H(x,K)=r\}=0,
 \qquad r\ge0.                                                               \tag{18}
\]
The case \(r=0\) was proved in the preceding paragraph.  Because a nondegenerate Gaussian has a Lebesgue density, its squared distance to \(K\) has no atoms.

The distribution is also strictly increasing on its positive support.  Each limit set contains a point, whereas moment separation puts the direction \(\mathbf1\) a positive distance from every secant or tangent direction.  Consequently distance along a suitable ray starting in the set is continuous, begins at zero, and tends to infinity.  Every nonempty open shell between two distance levels therefore has positive Gaussian probability.

Finally, if (9) failed, there would be \(\varepsilon_n\downarrow0\), levels \(x_n\in[0,M]\), and a sequence of geometries for which the displayed probability stayed above a fixed positive number.  Take the compactifying subsequence just constructed and also \(x_n\to x\).  Couple all Gaussian vectors as \(G_n=H_n^{1/2}Z\) with one \(Z\sim N_3(0,I_3)\).  Local Hausdorff convergence and Gaussian tightness imply
\[
 d_{H_n}(G_n,K_n)^2\longrightarrow d_H(H^{1/2}Z,K)^2
 \quad\text{in probability}.                                                 \tag{19}
\]
For any fixed \(\eta>0\), (19) bounds the offending probability by \(o(1)+\Pr(|d_H(H^{1/2}Z,K)^2-x|\le\eta)\).  Letting \(\eta\downarrow0\) contradicts (18).  This proves (9).  The same coupling, atomlessness, and strict increase show that quantiles converge along every compactifying sequence.  Sequential compactness then makes the extension uniformly continuous.

added_lemmas.statement:
For each fixed \(N\) and allowed observed design, \(\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}\) is compact.  The law of
\[
 d_{H_N}(G_N+\lambda q_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2
\]
is atomless and has a strictly increasing distribution function on \((0,\infty)\); its \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile is continuous in \((\lambda,p)\).  Hence the maximum defining \(c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\) is attained and
\[
 \inf_{(\lambda,p)\in\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}}
 \Pr\{d_{H_N}(G_N+\lambda q_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2
       \le c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\}=1-\alpha.                           \tag{20}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 0<c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\le\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha},                       \tag{21}
\]
and both bounds are uniform over the allowed designs after compactification.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The legal spectral tuples form a closed subset of the compact product of the amplitude interval, exponent interval, and nuisance compactum: for each fixed \(\omega\), the determinant inequality is closed, and intersection over \(\omega\in\mathbb R^d\) preserves closedness.  The map from such a tuple to
\[
 \left(\frac{AK_d(p)\sqrt N h_N^{2p-1}}{\sqrt{c_Xc_W}},p\right)
\]
is continuous because \(h_N,c_X,c_W,K_d(p)>0\).  Its image \(\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}\) is therefore compact.

The atomlessness and strict increase are the finite-\(N\) cases proved in the compactification lemma.  If \((\lambda_n,p_n)\to(\lambda,p)\), coupling with the same \(G_N\) and using continuity of \(q_N\) gives almost-sure convergence of the displayed statistic.  Atomlessness gives convergence of its distribution functions at every threshold.  Strict increase then gives convergence of the unique \((1-\alpha)\)-quantiles: if a subsequence of quantiles stayed below or above the limiting quantile, evaluation at an intermediate continuity point would contradict the definition of a quantile.  Thus the quantile map is continuous, and compactness makes its maximum attainable.

Let \((\lambda_*,p_*)\) be a maximizer.  Every parameter pair has probability at least \(1-\alpha\) at the maximum critical value, while continuity and strict increase give probability exactly \(1-\alpha\) for the maximizing pair.  This proves (20).

For (21), the cone contains the complete line \(\{bq_N(p):b\in\mathbb R\}\).  Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d_{H_N}(G_N+\lambda q_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2
 &\le \inf_{b\in\mathbb R}
   \|G_N+\lambda q_N(p)-bq_N(p)\|_{H_N}^2\\
 &=\inf_{a\in\mathbb R}\|G_N-aq_N(p)\|_{H_N}^2.
 \end{aligned}                                                               \tag{22}
\]
After whitening, the last expression is the squared Euclidean norm of the projection of a standard three-dimensional Gaussian onto a two-dimensional subspace, hence has the \(\chi^2_2\) distribution.  This proves the upper bound.  Positivity and its uniform version follow from atomlessness at zero, strict increase, and the compactification argument: a sequence of zero or vanishing \((1-\alpha)\)-quantiles would have a compactified limit with positive probability at distance zero, contrary to (18).

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For a legal spectral parameter tuple \(\xi=(A,c_X,c_W,\alpha_X,\alpha_W,\alpha_C,p)\), form the physical set \(\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}\), the Gaussian reference critical value \(c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\), and its certified outward approximation \(\overline c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\).  The finite-dimensional profile set is
\[
 \widetilde C_N
 =\{b\in\mathcal B:T_N(b)\le \overline c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\}.
\]
For certification, write \(G_N=H_N^{1/2}Z\), \(Z\sim N_3(0,I_3)\), truncate \(Z\) to a cube using the explicit Gaussian tail bound, eliminate the line loading analytically or bound it by coercivity, and subdivide the resulting finite boxes in \((\lambda,p,r,b,Z)\).  Outward interval evaluations of \(q_N\), \(H_N^{-1}\), and the quadratic distance objective give lower and upper probability sums.  Bisection in the threshold continues until the certified critical-value bracket has width at most \(N^{-1}\); its upper endpoint, capped by \(\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}\), is \(\overline c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\).  The physical set itself is enclosed by interval subdivision of the compact spectral parameter set and of the one-dimensional radial determinant constraint.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The former handle did not define the physical parameter set, the attainable critical value, the reported confidence set, or the certified finite computation required by the resolved calibration theorem.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(\widetilde C_N=\{b\in\mathcal B:N\widehat\gamma_N^{-1}d_{H_N}(m_N-b\mathbf1,\{a q_N(r):a\in\mathbb R,\ r\in[p_{\min},p_{\max}]\})^2\le\overline c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\}\), where \(\overline c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\) is a certified outward \(N^{-1}\)-approximation to the supremum, over the legal physical set \(\Lambda_N^{\mathrm{phys}}\), of the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(d_{H_N}(G_N+\lambda q_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2\).
proposed_core_edits.reason: The resolved theorem makes the attainable certified profile set, rather than only the conservative chi-square set, the coverage-facing functional.

prose_updates.tldr: Three exact affine-annihilating local slopes separate the causal homogeneous slope from a signed Mat\'ern cross-tail even when its amplitude vanishes and its exponent is unidentified. The actual-design Gaussian experiment and feasible scale studentization support an attainable, design-specific Gaussian profile critical value whose compactified quantile is continuous through zero, strong-amplitude tangent limits, exponent endpoints, and the one-dimensional physical elbow. A certified outward interval computation yields asymptotic lower-envelope coverage exactly \(1-\alpha\), root-\(N\) diameter and risk, while an exact observed-field Gaussian two-point/KL argument gives matching squared-risk and arbitrary-honest-confidence-set expected-diameter lower bounds.

project_justification.gap: Existing spatial fixed-domain theory does not provide uniform coverage through a vanishing signed cross-tail on changing quasi-uniform designs, and generic weak-identification theory does not determine the physically attainable tangent and endpoint calibration for this cone.
project_justification.niche: The note treats only the no-nugget, exact Mat\'ern-smoothness-one-half, deterministic quasi-uniform \(d\le2\) model with a compact parametric signed cross-tail. In that class, exact affine stencils make the observed-design mean curve and covariance geometry finite-dimensional and computable.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the actual-design Gaussian experiment, feasible residual-scale studentization, continuous attainable Gaussian-tube calibration with certified upper approximation, exact asymptotic \(1-\alpha\) lower-envelope coverage, root-\(N\) diameter and squared-risk upper bounds, and matching exact observed-field Gaussian two-point/KL lower bounds.

prose_updates.related_work: Keshavarz, Nguyen and Scott analyze local inversion-free covariance estimation on irregular spatial designs, and Datta and Stein study consistent spatial-slope estimation; neither provides the attainable profile calibration proved here. Li (2022) studies Bayesian fixed-domain posterior behavior and a Bernstein--von Mises limit for covariance parameters, rather than this frequentist signed-cross-tail slope experiment. Andrews and Mikusheva provide generic weak-identification tools, but not the changing curved cone, physical elbow, or certified continuum optimization. Gneiting, Kleiber and Schlather provide the valid multivariate Mat\'ern spectral family. Burman, Ogburn and Datta supply the conditional PM2.5/COVID county-centroid homogeneous-slope consumer when the note's Gaussian Mat\'ern and quasi-uniform design diagnostics hold.
prose_updates.honest_scope: All upper guarantees are restricted to the stated no-nugget, exact Mat\'ern-smoothness-one-half Gaussian model, its compact parametric signed cross-tail, deterministic quasi-uniform designs, and \(d\in\{1,2\}\). They do not cover unknown marginal smoothness, nugget effects, random or broader covariance classes, or efficiency constants. The certified numerical statement uses convergent outward interval representations of the fixed model specification and observed coordinates. The lower bound is proved by an exact observed-field Gaussian two-point/KL calculation on the \(A=0\) Mat\'ern-half submodel and transfers to a broader anchor class only after that class is formally shown to contain this submodel. The Burman--Ogburn--Datta application remains conditional on the stated diagnostics and does not enlarge the mathematical model.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem closes the former distinction between conservative chi-square honesty and attainable exact lower-envelope coverage without estimating the unidentified exponent at zero amplitude.
statement_notes.gap: The new work is the uniform compactification and anti-concentration over actual designs, together with physical-regime-aware certified continuum optimization; these pieces are absent from generic conditional-size results.
statement_notes.consumer: It supplies the coverage-facing profile set for the stated county-centroid homogeneous-slope analysis, conditional on the exact model and design diagnostics.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(0<\alpha<1/2\), there are constants \(c_{\alpha},c>0\) such that every sequence \((I_N)_{N\geq 1}\) of measurable random subsets of \(\mathbb R\), with measurable diameter \(\operatorname{diam}(I_N)=\sup\{|u-v|:u,v\in I_N\}\) and \(\operatorname{diam}(\varnothing)=0\), satisfying
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\inf_{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M}
 P_N\{\beta\in I_N\}\geq 1-\alpha,
\]
obeys
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\sqrt N
 \sup_{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M}
 E_{P_N}[\operatorname{diam}(I_N)]\geq c_{\alpha}.
\]
Moreover, every estimator sequence \((\widetilde\beta_N)_{N\geq1}\) obeys
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}N
 \sup_{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M}
 E_{P_N}[(\widetilde\beta_N-\beta)^2]\geq c.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(\nu=(d+1)/2\).  We construct a two-point subexperiment inside the model class.  Fix an admissible deterministic design sequence and a nuisance tuple \((c_X,c_W,\alpha_X,\alpha_W,\alpha_C)\in\mathcal K_{\mathrm{nuis}}\).  Fix also \(p^\circ\in[p_{\min},p_{\max}]\) and set \(A=0\), which is permitted by the amplitude-space assumption.  The determinant-margin assumption on the nonempty model implies \(0<\rho\leq1\), because
\[
 0\leq \frac{f_{XW}(\omega)^2}{f_X(\omega)f_W(\omega)}
 \leq 1-\rho
\]
for every member and every \(\omega\).  Hence, at \(A=0\),
\[
 f_X(\omega)f_W(\omega)-f_{XW}(\omega)^2
 =f_X(\omega)f_W(\omega)
 \geq\rho f_X(\omega)f_W(\omega).
 \tag{1}
\]
The marginal spectra are positive and integrable: near the origin they are bounded, while their radial integrands at infinity are of order \(r^{d-1}r^{-(d+1)}=r^{-2}\).  Their inverse Fourier transforms therefore define stationary covariance kernels.  For every finite collection of sites and coefficients, the corresponding covariance quadratic form is the integral of the positive spectrum times the squared modulus of a finite exponential sum, and hence is nonnegative.  The consistent centered Gaussian finite-dimensional distributions with these kernels define independent centered stationary Gaussian fields \(X\) and \(W\).  Together with (1), the spectral-family assumption, and \(Y=\beta X+W\), this produces an admissible \(A=0\) submodel of \(\mathcal M\) for every \(\beta\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal B)\).  The parameter \(p^\circ\) is immaterial on this submodel, so no identification of \(p\) is being assumed.

For the fixed nuisance tuple define
\[
 C_\star=\frac{c_X}{c_W}
 \max\left\{1,\left(\frac{\alpha_W^2}{\alpha_X^2}\right)^\nu\right\}.
 \tag{2}
\]
Nuisance compactness places every coordinate in \((0,\infty)\), so \(0<C_\star<\infty\).  The two marginal spectra satisfy, pointwise,
\[
 \frac{f_X(\omega)}{f_W(\omega)}
 =\frac{c_X}{c_W}
 \left(\frac{\alpha_W^2+\|\omega\|^2}
 {\alpha_X^2+\|\omega\|^2}\right)^\nu
 \leq C_\star.
 \tag{3}
\]
Let \(X_N=(X(s_{1,N}),\ldots,X(s_{N,N}))^{\mathsf T}\), define \(W_N\) analogously, and denote their covariance matrices by \(\Sigma_{X,N}\) and \(\Sigma_{W,N}\).  The spectral representation and (3) imply, for every \(z\in\mathbb R^N\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 z^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_{X,N}z
 &=\kappa_d\int_{\mathbb R^d}f_X(\omega)
 \left|\sum_{i=1}^Nz_i e^{\mathrm i\omega^{\mathsf T}s_{i,N}}\right|^2\,d\omega\\
 &\leq C_\star\kappa_d\int_{\mathbb R^d}f_W(\omega)
 \left|\sum_{i=1}^Nz_i e^{\mathrm i\omega^{\mathsf T}s_{i,N}}\right|^2\,d\omega
 =C_\star z^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_{W,N}z,
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{4}
\]
where the Fourier-normalization constant \(\kappa_d>0\) is the same for both fields.  The separation assumption makes the sites distinct.  If \(z\neq0\), choose a vector \(v\in\mathbb R^d\) outside the finite union of hyperplanes orthogonal to the site differences.  Then the numbers \(v^{\mathsf T}s_{i,N}\) are distinct.  Were the exponential sum in (4) identically zero, its restrictions to \(\omega=tv\) and its first \(N\) derivatives at \(t=0\) would give a nonsingular Vandermonde system forcing \(z=0\), a contradiction.  Thus the sum is nonzero on an open set.  Since \(f_W>0\), its integral is strictly positive.  Therefore \(\Sigma_{W,N}\) is invertible and
\[
 \Sigma_{X,N}\preceq C_\star\Sigma_{W,N}.
 \tag{5}
\]
If \(\lambda_{1,N},\ldots,\lambda_{N,N}\) are the eigenvalues of
\(\Sigma_{X,N}^{1/2}\Sigma_{W,N}^{-1}\Sigma_{X,N}^{1/2}\), then (5), by congruence with \(\Sigma_{W,N}^{-1/2}\) and equality of the nonzero spectra of the two matrix products, yields
\[
 0<\lambda_{i,N}\leq C_\star,
 \qquad
 \sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_{i,N}
 =\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_{W,N}^{-1}\Sigma_{X,N})
 \leq NC_\star.
 \tag{6}
\]

Choose \(\beta_0\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal B)\).  For fixed \(q>0\), let
\[
 \Delta_N=qN^{-1/2},\qquad \beta_{1,N}=\beta_0+\Delta_N.
 \tag{7}
\]
Because \(\beta_0\) is interior, \(\beta_{1,N}\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal B)\) for all sufficiently large \(N\).  Let \(P_{0,N}\) and \(P_{1,N}\) be the two \(A=0\) observed-field laws at slopes \(\beta_0\) and \(\beta_{1,N}\), respectively, with all other quantities fixed.  For each \(N\), the second law is the \(N\)-th marginal of a member of \(\mathcal M\) obtained by holding \(\beta_{1,N}\) fixed over that member's entire sample-size sequence.  Thus both alternatives are available to the supremum and infimum defining the theorem.

Under \(P_{0,N}\), \(X_N\) and \(W_N=Y_N-\beta_0X_N\) are independent centered Gaussian vectors.  Conditional on \(X_N\), changing the slope by \(\Delta_N\) changes the conditional mean of \(Y_N\) by \(\Delta_NX_N\) and leaves its covariance equal to \(\Sigma_{W,N}\).  Consequently the exact likelihood ratio on the complete observed vector \((X_N,Y_N)\) is
\[
 L_N:=\frac{dP_{1,N}}{dP_{0,N}}
 =\exp\left\{\Delta_NX_N^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_{W,N}^{-1}W_N
 -\frac{\Delta_N^2}{2}X_N^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_{W,N}^{-1}X_N\right\}.
 \tag{8}
\]
In particular, independence and centering give the exact divergence
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_{0,N},P_{1,N})
 =\frac{\Delta_N^2}{2}
 \operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_{W,N}^{-1}\Sigma_{X,N})
 \leq\frac{q^2C_\star}{2}.
 \tag{9}
\]
For the sharper total-variation constant used below, condition (8) on \(X_N\).  The Gaussian moment-generating identity gives
\[
 E_{0,N}[L_N^2\mid X_N]
 =\exp\{\Delta_N^2X_N^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_{W,N}^{-1}X_N\}.
\]
Diagonalizing this Gaussian quadratic form yields, whenever \(2\Delta_N^2C_\star<1\),
\[
 E_{0,N}L_N^2
 =\prod_{i=1}^N(1-2\Delta_N^2\lambda_{i,N})^{-1/2}.
 \tag{10}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(N\), \(2q^2C_\star/N\leq1/2\).  Since \(-\log(1-x)\leq2x\) for \(0\leq x\leq1/2\), equations (6), (7), and (10) imply
\[
 \log E_{0,N}L_N^2
 \leq\frac{2q^2}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_{i,N}
 \leq2q^2C_\star.
 \tag{11}
\]
By the definition of total variation and Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(P_{0,N},P_{1,N})
 =\frac12E_{0,N}|L_N-1|
 \leq\frac12\{E_{0,N}(L_N-1)^2\}^{1/2}
 \leq\frac12\{e^{2q^2C_\star}-1\}^{1/2}.
 \tag{12}
\]
This bound concerns the actual observed-field likelihood and does not posit independent Fourier coordinates.

We first prove the confidence-set assertion.  Put \(\eta_\alpha=1-2\alpha>0\), using the nominal-level assumption, and choose
\[
 q_\alpha=left\{\frac{1}{2C_\star}
 \log\left(1+\frac{\eta_\alpha^2}{4}\right)\right\}^{1/2}>0.
 \tag{13}
\]
Equation (12) gives \(\operatorname{TV}(P_{0,N},P_{1,N})\leq\eta_\alpha/4\) eventually.  For an arbitrary candidate sequence of measurable random sets define
\[
 a_N=\inf_{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M}P_N\{\beta\in I_N\}.
\]
Honesty gives \(\liminf_Na_N\geq1-\alpha\).  Total variation and the union bound give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{0,N}\{\beta_0,\beta_{1,N}\in I_N\}
 &\geq P_{0,N}\{\beta_0\in I_N\}
       +P_{0,N}\{\beta_{1,N}\in I_N\}-1\\
 &\geq 2a_N-1-\operatorname{TV}(P_{0,N},P_{1,N}).
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{14}
\]
On the event in (14), the definition of diameter and (7) give \(\operatorname{diam}(I_N)\geq\Delta_N\), without any connectedness assumption on \(I_N\).  It follows from (13)--(14) that
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\sqrt N
 \sup_{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M}
 E_{P_N}[\operatorname{diam}(I_N)]
 &\geq q_\alpha\liminf_{N\to\infty}
 P_{0,N}\{\beta_0,\beta_{1,N}\in I_N\}\\
 &\geq \frac34q_\alpha\eta_\alpha
 =:c_\alpha>0.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{15}
\]

Finally, let \(\widetilde\beta_N\) be any estimator and take
\[
 q_0=\left(\frac{\log2}{2C_\star}\right)^{1/2}.
\]
Equation (12) gives \(\operatorname{TV}(P_{0,N},P_{1,N})\leq1/2\) eventually.  Define
\(\phi_N=\mathbf 1\{\widetilde\beta_N\geq(\beta_0+\beta_{1,N})/2\}\).  On \(\{\phi_N=1\}\) under \(P_{0,N}\), the squared error is at least \(\Delta_N^2/4\); on \(\{\phi_N=0\}\) under \(P_{1,N}\), it is at least the same amount.  If
\(R_{k,N}=E_{k,N}[(\widetilde\beta_N-\beta_{k,N})^2]\), with \(\beta_{0,N}=\beta_0\), then the definition of total variation gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \max(R_{0,N},R_{1,N})
 &\geq\frac{\Delta_N^2}{8}
 \{P_{0,N}(\phi_N=1)+P_{1,N}(\phi_N=0)\}\\
 &\geq\frac{\Delta_N^2}{8}
 \{1-\operatorname{TV}(P_{0,N},P_{1,N})\}
 \geq\frac{q_0^2}{16N}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{16}
\]
Both alternatives lie in \(\mathcal M\), so (16) yields
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}N
 \sup_{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M}
 E_{P_N}[(\widetilde\beta_N-\beta)^2]
 \geq\frac{q_0^2}{16}
 =\frac{\log2}{32C_\star}=:c>0.
\]
Together with (15), this proves both lower bounds.
added_lemmas.justification: The exact observed-field Gaussian two-point experiment proves the honest expected-diameter and squared-risk lower bounds without requiring identification of \(p\) at zero amplitude.
added_lemmas.gap: Scalar microergodic limits and abstract modulus theory do not by themselves provide this lower bound for arbitrary confidence sets in the complete bivariate observed-field experiment.
added_lemmas.consumer: The result certifies that no spatial adjustment can uniformly improve on root-\(N\) confidence-set diameter or \(N^{-1}\) squared risk over the stated no-nugget model.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The interval-only statement is obsolete because the same exact observed-field Gaussian argument proves the strictly stronger expected-diameter lower bound for arbitrary measurable confidence sets while retaining the estimator squared-risk lower bound; migrating inbound edges preserves every former consequence.
